newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan April bankruptcy debt hits record high.
newsitem.headline: Japan April bankruptcy debt hits record high.

text.p: Total debts held by Japanese companies that went bankrupt in April hit a monthly record high of 2.62 trillion yen ($22.5 billion), up 525.2 percent from a year earlier, research company Tokyo Shoko Research Ltd said on Thursday.
The debts were up 84 percent from the previous month, Tokyo Shoko said in its monthly bankruptcy report.
A total of 1,432 companies went bankrupt in April, up 20 percent from a year earlier and up 4.2 percent from March, Tokyo Shoko said.
"Listed companies and over-the-counter (OTC) companies have been going bankrupt one after another since the beginning of the year," Tokyo Shoko said.
The majority of bankruptcies in April were due to recession-related conditions such as sluggish sales, accumulated losses and unpaid bills, it said.

Tokyo Shoko said the main reason for the large increase in debt was the unprecedentedly large bankruptcies of three nonbank financial firms -- Crown Leasing Corp, Nippon Total Finance Inc and Nippon Assurance Finance Services Co. All three were affiliated with troubled long-term credit bank Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB), it said.
Total debt of the three firms, which were declared bankrupt in early April, was 2.03 trillion yen ($17.5 billion).
Crown Leasing had the largest debt among the three at 1.19 trillion yen ($10.2 billion), which marked the largest bankruptcy ever.
"There is still a long way to go, considering that the biggest bankruptcy ever took place right at the beginning of the 1997 business year (which started on April 1)," Tokyo Shoko said.
It said the hardest-hit industry in April was construction, due to increasing competition for orders after a fall in public works spending.
Bankruptcies of contractors rose 32.8 percent year-on-year to 421 cases, up for the seventh consecutive month.

The number of business failures in the wholesale sector was the second-highest and those in manufacturing were the third-highest, with year-on-year increases of 28.1 percent in wholesaling and 14.7 percent in manufacturing.
A total of six finance and insurance companies failed in April, up 50 percent year-on-year.

Tokyo Shoko said it expects bankruptcies to rise further due to Japan's prolonged economic slump and problems of non-performing assets caused by the bursting of Japan's "bubble" of inflated asset prices in the late 1980s. ($=116 yen)
